articleTitle: Optimum design of millimeter-wave impatt diode oscillators
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An oscillator model used to investigate the dynamic behaviors of millimeter-wave pulsed and CW oscillators was developed. The effect of external influences on device behavior and oscillator performance techniques to control the post turn-on frequency drift were described.

articleTitle: Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) of compact toroid plasmas
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Compact toroids have in the past been characterized by high plasma density and low magnetic fields, and hence, have not been accessible for ECRH experiments. However, the MS Spheromak planned for construction at the University of Maryland will alleviate this situation having B ∼20kG and n ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. We calculate good transmission to the center of the MS Spheromak plasma and almost complete absorption at the 2nd harmonic of the electron cyclotron frequency. Absorption in Spheromaks is much stronger than in Tokamaks because of the flatter magnetic field profile. A gyrotron at 100 GHz, 500 kW, and τ≲1 msec would be suitable for a significant experimental demonstration.

articleTitle: Field analysis and performance predictions of complex cavity gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The use of complex or stepped cavities for gyrotron oscillators to allow higher order mode operation while enjoying the reduced mode competition advantages of lower order mode devices have been experimentally demonstrated. The results of computer analyses of complex cavities with both TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> and higher mode prebunchers will be shown. Methods of tapering electic field profiles, controlling cavity links, relative field strengths and Q-factors will be discussed. Computed efficiencies and start oscillation thresholds for several different cavities will be shown. Practical problems to be expected in machining and high power testing will be addressed.

articleTitle: Far-infrared imaging of the sun with a balloon-borne 60 cm Ø telescope
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Complete solar images at the wavelengths 50 μm, 80 μm and 200 μm were taken with a balloon-borne 60 cm ⊘ Cassegrain telescope from a height of 38 km on April 30, 1983. Maps of the solar brightness temperature are presented and compared with vis, Hα and Call K solar images.

articleTitle: A 3-mm maser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A resonant maser has been developed for the frequency range 85 to 95 GHz. The active material of the maser are natural single-crystals of andalusite, and the push-pull pumping has been employed. The gain achieved over a 30 MHz band width is 20 dB, with moderate pumping powers.

articleTitle: Application of Gyratrons to large troidal device
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Electron cyclotron heating experiments have been performed in Heliotron E device to produce and heat the high temperature plasma. Varian VGE 8053 Gyratrons provide 300–400 kw, 53.2 GHz microwave to the vacuum chamber. The typical plasma parameters obtained are T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 1.5 keV, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 1–3 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. The heating rates are 6–10 eV/kw and 6–8 J/kw. These values are 1–2 times larger than that of tokamaks. At the conference, operational techniques of gyratrons, included power supply and wave guide systems, will also be presented.

articleTitle: Advances in submillimeter carcinotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two new types of carcinotrons are described in this paper :— A 600 GHz tube delivering 10 to 20 mW,— An 850 to 1 000 GHz tube delivering a few milliwatts. The performances of several tubes of chis type are given. The feasibility of higher frequency tubes is discussed.

articleTitle: A Schottky Barrier Diode detector and laser diagnostic system for the F.I.R.
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We wish to report on the design and performance of a point contact Schottky Barrier Diode detector and laser/microwave heterodyne diagnostic system. A detector has been optimized for the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F, 496 μm emission and measurements will be presented on the NEP and detector bandwidth.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of the ir water-vapor absorption
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: New results on the temperature dependence of the controversial water-vapor continuum absorption within the 8–14 μm atmospheric window are presented. Laboratory measurements have been performed by the aid of a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser photoacoustic system.

articleTitle: Second- and third-harmonic operation of a gyrotron backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: First measurements are presented of electrical tuning and output power characteristics for a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-mode gyro-BWO operating at the second and third cyclotron harmonics.

articleTitle: Theory on distributed feedback lasers with strong modulation
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel calculation of resonance frequencies and threshold gains of distributed feedback (DFB) lasers with strong modulations is presented. Starting from dispersion relations of infinite DFB structures it applies the concepts of theories on Perot-Fabry resonators and energy-band calculations.

articleTitle: Broadband measurements of permittivity and permeability
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Theory and system designs from multiple band measurements of permittivity and permeability will be presented. Measured data will be presented for various microwave absorbers from 5–100 GHz. An analysis of system errors is also presented.

articleTitle: New magneto-optic effect on the spectral thermal infrared emission from ferromagnets
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: IN 1977 MUELLER, FUCHS AND KNEUBUEHL DISCOVFRED THE PARTIAL CIRCULAR POLARIZATION OF THE SPECTRAL THERMAL EMISSION FROM AXIALLY MAGNETIZED FERROMAGNETS. NOW, WE HAVE ORSERBED A RELATED EFFECT, THE PARTIALLY LINEAR POLARIZATION OF THE EMISSION FROM IRON MAGNETIZED TO ITS SURFACE. WHILE THE PARTIAL CIRCULAR POLARIZATION IP PROPORTIONAL. TO THE MAGNETIZATION. THE PARTIAL LINEAR POLARIZATION SHOWS A QUADRATIC DEPENDENCE IN A FIRST APPROXIMATION.

articleTitle: Helical distributed feedback Gaslaser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Theory, realization and mode characteristics of a helical distributed feedback far-ir gas laser are presented. In this laser DFB is provided by a structure of helical symmetry contrary to standard DFB lasers which are based on linear periodic modulations.

articleTitle: Limiting beam current in gyrotrons due to space charge depression
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Gyrotrons operating at millimeter wavelengths in megawatt power levels will require electron beam currents of tens of amperes in highly overmoded cavities. The limiting current will be determined by space charge depression, either by modifying the velocity space loss cone to produce mirroring or by causing the Brillouim limit to be exceeded. Our computer simulations have demonstrated that previous estimates of the limiting current are overly pessimistic. Comparative results will be presented.

articleTitle: Computer aided design of inverted strip dielectric waveguide millimeter-wave couplers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A computer aided design technique has been developed for the design of beam splitter coupler and distributed type coupler using inverted strip dielectric waveguides. The optical beam principle has been used for the beam splitter coupler. Numerical results for these couplers at 80 GHz with minimum directivity of 30 dB and VSWR of 1.15 have been presented.

articleTitle: Multiphoton transitions in free electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Interrelation between quantum and classical regimes of operation of free electron lasers is studied using the correspondence principle. The developed theory is applicable in both regimes and significantly simplifies the traditional calculation of the small signal gain in the laser. Application of the theory to different laser configurations will be presented.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional theory of Ubitron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A three-dimensional theory of the Ubitron/FEL type devices is presented, taking into consideration the transverse variation of the wiggler field, finite waveguide geometry and space charge effects. A dispersion relation to calculate linear gain is obtained by solving Vlasov equation and Maxwell's equations.

articleTitle: A grazing incidence far-infrared laser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The introduction of gratings at grazing incidence in tunable dye lasers improved considerably their performance. In this paper we present the first grazing incidence far-ir gas laser, its characteristics and relations to distributed feedback gas lasers.

articleTitle: Non-linear photoconductivity of Cd1-xMnxSe
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Pulsed FIR photoconductance at 385 um and 94 μm is found to saturate at high power levels (∼ 1 kW peak power, 150 ns pulse width). The response is fit to a rate model giving an inelastic scattering time of ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup>s. The technique should have general application.

articleTitle: Session guided propagation and devices: Propagation along circular guide containing passive semiconductor magnetoplasma
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An analytical technique is developed and applied to calculate and interpret the nonreciprocal transmission characteristics of a circular guide, containing passive semiconductor magneto-plasma. Possible applications of the structure for construction of practical nonreciprocal control devices for millimeter wavelengths are discussed.

articleTitle: Slotted gyrotron cavities
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Computer simulations predict that narrow, longitudinal slots in the walls of a gyrotron cavity tend not to affect modes such as the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,5</inf> while lowering the Q factor of competing modes. Available experimental data' from cold test cavities will be presented.

articleTitle: Lasers: Self modulation properties of miniature CO2 TEA lasers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A theory is presented, with supporting experimental data, to explain how temporal gain switch pulse degradation occurs in miniature CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> TEA lasers. The theory provides a mathematical relationship between the laser cavity parameters and the period of modulation of the gain switch pulse.

articleTitle: A novel method for measuring pulsed phase noise, with an application in W-band
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel method is described to measure pulsed phase noise. Experimental details involved in measuring the noise of a pulsed IMPATT source at 92.3 GHz are presented. A brief discussion is given on the different requirements for stationary(slow moving) transmitter platforms and fast moving platforms(aircraft) with large ‘zero’ Doppler frequency. The use of the Delay Line discriminator as a ‘de-chirping’ circuit is pointed out, though no experimental data is available at this time.

articleTitle: Fir radiation of the UCSB-FEL
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We present here calculations of the free electron laser spontaneous emission inside a rectangular waveguide and the techniques that will be employed to measure power and bandwidth above and below laser threshold in the FIR region.

articleTitle: Experiments on submillimeter-wave gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In this report results of experimental investigation of submillimeter-wave gyrotrons with pulsed solenoids will be presented. At wavelengths 0.5–0.65 mm the output power of 60–80 kW is achieved with efficiency 8–10%. The output power is transformed to the wave beam with quasi-linear polarization. Methods of the wavelength and polarization measurement will be described.

articleTitle: ECE diagnosis of tokamak edge temperature
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: ECE is well established as a diagnostic for tokamak core temperature. We present an evaluation of the extension of standard techniques to the low-temperature, low-density. edge plasma. Included are the effects of optical depth, harmonic overlap, and spatial resolution.

articleTitle: ECE experiments on Heliotron E device
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Electron cyclotron heating experiments have been perfomed in Heliotron E device to produce and heat the high temperature plasma. Varian VGE 8G50 Gyratrons provide 300–400 kw, 53.2 GKz microwave to the vacuum chamber. The typical plasma parameters obtained are T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> =1.5 keV, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 1–3 × 10 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. The heating rates are 6–10 eV/kw and 6–8 J/kw. These values are 1–2 times larger than that of tokamaks.

articleTitle: Parametric evaluation of the Fabry-Perot interferometer in millimeter permittivity and permeability measurements
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The precision of measurements of complex electromagnetic material parameters is examined as a function of fabricationn tolerances and of the values to be measured. The precision is compared to that of various free space and waveguide measurement configurations.

articleTitle: Future infrared-laser particle accelerators
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Theory and feasibility of ir and near-mm laser particle accelerators making use of linear and helical DFB structures are discussed with respect to other proposed laser accelerators, e.g. the laser-driven grating linac.

articleTitle: The Lens relay as a method of E.C.E. transportation
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: As an alternative to waveguide, a lens relay may be used to carry E.C.E. from the plasma to analysing equipment. Experimental results evolving microwave and visible radiation, in addition to those from a variable wavelength gaussian beam simulator, will be presented.

articleTitle: Vertical ground-based radiometric observations of the atmosphere at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A series of measurements of the atmosphere with ground-based radiometers is described. Radiometers at 94, 130 and 183 GHz have been employed. The 183 GHz radiometer has three double-sidebands on the sides of the water vapor line. The results of calculations for both long-term and short-term effects are presented.

articleTitle: Field attenuation measurements at 0.89 mm
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Field measurements of clear atmosphere attenuation have been made at a wavelenght of 0.89 mm, using an optically pumped far infrared laser as a source. Absolute measurements of attenuation idicated 4 to ]4 8B/km above values calculated by absorption line compilations. Attenuation sensitivity measurements yielded values 1.5 to 2.0 times greater that the slopes predicted by monomer theory. Reasonable agreement is obtained with previously measured data by Tanton and by Ryadov and Furashov.

articleTitle: Frequency tuning of far-infrared radiation on hot excitons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Generation of far-infrared radiation by hot excitons in semiconductors (CdS) has been recently obtained experimentally on a large amount of transitions. It is shown theoretically that selection of separate lines can be achieved, in particular, by lowering temperature to ≤4.2K (herewith many of lines those intensities depend on the exciton wave vector would disappear) and by the use of different induced lattices of exciton states inverse population. Tuning is achievable by pressure, applied magnetic field and changing excitation level.

articleTitle: NRL quasi-optical gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 100 kW proof of principle experiment has been assembled. The quasi-optical cavity is designed to resonate at a frequency of 115 GHz (λ = 2.6 mm, |B| = 41 kG) with an efficiency of 25%. Recent developments and experimental results will be discussed.

articleTitle: Transmission of silicon from 0.1–1 mm wavelength
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Although silicon has been used for many years as a far infrared material, there is surprisingly little quantitative data on its transmission [1]. Birch [2] has provided accurate data on the refractive index and reflectivity of n-silicon in the 0.1–1 mm region. He also measured the power absorption coefficient of the single crystal sample that he was using. However, as it was not relevant to his experiment, he made no accurate determination of the sample resistivity which had a nominal value of 1000 ohm-cm.

articleTitle: Properties of an open structure mixer at 584 GHz and GHz
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A submillimeter heterodyne receiver with a Schottky barrier diode in a open structure mixer has been investigated at 584 GHz and 803 GHz. Working at room temperature a single sideband system noise temperature of 5,950 K and 11,700 K respectively has been achieved.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave ubitron experimental design
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A broadband, 35GHz ubitron experiment is being assembled at NRL with the aid of a new 3-0 theory. The experiment will utilize a high-power, high-quality Pierce gun, and a bifilar helix wiggler. Details concerning the selection of parameters and the design of equipment will be presented.

articleTitle: A gyrotron-backward-wave-amplifier experiment
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A proof-of-principle experimental device of a gyrotron backward-wave amplifier has been designed and is being fabricated. The TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>-mode device is electronically tunable over 18 to 26 GHz with an instantaneous bandwidth 1 to 3%. The possibility of enhanced bandwidth will be investigated by using a tapered waveguide in a tapered magnetic field.

articleTitle: Current oscillations in p-i-n diodes at interband photoexcitation
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The dynamics of photoexcited electron-hole plasma in p-i-n diodes under steady applied voltage and photogeneration is investigated by the Monte Carlo particle simulation. The current oscillations with the frequency of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> – 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> Hz at the ballistic transport conditions are obtained.

articleTitle: New results on tapered slot endfire antennas on dielectric substsates
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Tapered slot endfire antennas for millimeter wave single beam and imaging applications have been investigated systematically. Gain, beamwidth, efficiency, coupling impedance and bandwidth have been determined experimentally for various shapes, such as linearly tapered (LISA), exponentially tapered (Vivaldi) and constant width (CWSA). Substrates of both high and low dielectric constants have been included. This class of antenna elements appears very attractive for a number of applications, and is easy to fabricate.

articleTitle: Imaging system at 94 GHz using tapered slot antenna elements
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 94 GHz Imaging System using linearly tapered slot antennas with integrated beamlead diodes as receptor elements has been developed. The elements have sufficient gain to directly illuminate the sub-reflector of a Cassegrain antenna. The one-foot diameter of the main reflector determines a beam-width of 0.7 degrees for each beam. The measured spacing between adjacent beams in a seven element array is 0.64 degrees. A four element array has also been used for tracking.

articleTitle: Mode analysis of gyrotron radiation by far field measurements
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The possibility and convenience of identifying the mode composition at the output of high power gyrotrons and analyzing the mode conversion properties of overmoded waveguide components (tapers, bends, mode converters) by measuring the radiation pattern from an open-ended circular waveguide in the far field region are studied. The method has been simplified remarkably by using spatial correlations of the field amplitudes at selected angles.

articleTitle: Gain characteristics of stagger-tuned multicavity gyroklystron amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A linear theory of gyroklystron amplifiers has been formulated by solving an integral differential equation describing self-consistent gyrotron interaction in a series of cavities coupled by cutoff drift tubes. One can evaluate the gain versus frequency characteristics of gyroklystron designs which allow both mechanical and magnetic tuning of cavities.

articleTitle: High efficiency millimeter and submillimeter frequency multipliers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Frequency doublers, triplers and quadruplers operating from 90–570 GHz are described. Tripiers show a conversion efficiency of 16% at 100 GHz decreasing to ∼10% at 290 GHz, the doubler 7% efficiency at 570 GHz and the quadruplers ∼3% at 390 GHz. Devices are optimized for 10–20 mW input power and produce output powers of ∼l-5 mW.

articleTitle: A quasi-optical millimeter wave transmitter and receiver array for measurements of angular scintillation
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This system, used to measure the effects of atmospheric turbulence at frequencies between 116 and 173 GHz, comprises a front-fed, off-axis parabola transmitting antenna located 1.4 km from a receiver array. The five antennas in the latter receive local oscillator power from a phase-locked klystron source via a low-loss lens beam waveguide distribution system.

articleTitle: Superconducting tunnel junction receiver for 2.6 mm
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 110–118 GHz receiver based on a superconducting quasiparticle tunnel junction mixer is described. The single-sideband noise temperature is as low as 68 ± 3 K. This is nearly twice the sensitivity of any other receiver at this frequency.

articleTitle: Monolithic Schottky diode imaging arrays at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Monolithic GaAs Schottky diode imaging arrays have been demonstrated at 69 and 94 GHz. In the 94 GHz experiments, the diodes are fabricated by a self-aligning technique on semi-insulating GaAs and are isolated by a combination of a mesa-etch process and proton-bombardment. The series resistance is 20 ω and the estimated capacitance is 15–20 fF. The antennas are planar bow-ties, and power is coupled in through a quartz lens placed on the back of the GaAs substrate. The wafer is lapped to 90 μm thick to eliminate losses to substrate modes. The measured system responsivity is 330 V/W. The 69 GHz diodes are made by a non-self-aligned process, and a silicon substrate lens is used.

articleTitle: Measurements of phase noise spectra of selected millimeter wave klystrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: During a program whose objective is to measure millimeter wave atmospheric turbulence effects, the phase noise spectra of phase-locked klystron oscillators operating at 116, 140, and 173 GHz were measured. This paper describes the results obtained.

articleTitle: High-altitude atmospheric measurements at 92/183 GHz onboard the ER-2 research aircraft
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Airborne radiometric measurements have been performed onboard Lockheed's ER-2 aircraft. A multichannel imaging radiometer operating at 92/183 GHz was used in a series of flights over ocean, land, and along the Northern California coastline. Results from selected data flights are presented.

articleTitle: 60 GHz planar doped barrier subharmonic mixer
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 60 GHz planar doped barrier (PDB) subharmonically pumped mixer using 10 μm mesa diodes has been designed and fabricated using a new cross-guide mounting configuration. RF performance data using a 30 GHz local oscillator and a signal frequency of 59.5 GHz are discussed.

articleTitle: A high harmonic, low field gyrotron: Comparison between the cyclotron maser and peniotron-like interactions
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The highly efficient mth harmonic electron cyclotron maser interaction for a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m11</inf> gyrotron oscillator is compared with the (m-1)th harmonic peniotron-like interaction. Identical cavities and electron beams are used. Start oscillation conditions from weak field linear theory are given, as well as optimized non-linear efficiencies. The peniotron-like interaction leads to optimized efficiencies of ≲ 65%, while those for the electron cyclotron maser interaction are limited to ≲ 25% in the cases studied.

articleTitle: Chaos in SIS quasiparticle Tunneling
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An investigation into chaotic behavior in SIS quasiparticle currents is reported. The range of parameters for which period multiplying and chaos have been found to occur is discussed.

articleTitle: Infrared observations of the methanol C-O stretch band
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Many R and P branches in FTIR spectra of the C-O stretch band of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH have been assigned, including several in the first excited torsional state. IR-IR double resonance has confirmed that the Q(9,125) transition is pumped by the 9P(34) CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser line.

articleTitle: High-power pulsed operation of the NH3 laser on transitions between 100 and 300μm
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> laser pumped by a single mode, etalontuned TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser was optimized for operation on the 257 and 281μm transitions at power levels of 430 and 160 kW in 0.8μs pulses, respectively. Also, we report the first observation of 140 GHz laser action in NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at power levels up to 8 kW.

articleTitle: A millimeter wave radio frequency system for atmospheric turbulence measurements
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes a millimeter wave atmospheric transmission link operating at 116, 140 and 173 GHz designed to measure the mutual coherence function (MCF) for transmission through atmospheric turbulence. The transmitter and receiver local oscillator are phase-locked, and the receiver mixers are second harmonic types in the cross-guide configuration. The receiver uses double conversion, with intermediate frequencies of 930 and 30 MHz. A 30 MHz signal combining network uses phase shifters and video detectors to determine voltages proportional to the parameters required for determination of the MCF.

articleTitle: 13CH3F tunable Raman FIR laser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: It has previously been demonstrated that broad far-infrared tunability can be achieved by pumping <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F with a continuously-tunable high-power CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pump laser [1]. In those experiments, a ten-atmosphere CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pump laser provided 50 nsec output pulses which could be tuned continuously over a 450 GHz range from the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> 9R10 line to the 9R32 line, inclusively. This frequency range spans the R14 to R26 lines in the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> band of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F, and with pump pulse energies ranging from 100 to 150 m J, a FIR laser output was obtained over some 85% of the wavelength interval between 220 and 400 μm. At the optimum <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F pressure of 25–30 torr, the FIR output pulse energies were of the order of 0.1 mJ. The pump power density threshhold and the tuning curve (FIR output wavelength vs CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pump wavelength) were in good agreement with a theoretical model of laser emission via stimulated Raman scattering in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F developed by Biron et al [2].

articleTitle: Ka/Q band GaAs impatt amplifier technology
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: GaAs IMPATT diodes are capable of generating 2 to 3 W simultaneously with 18–22% efficiency in the 33 GHz to 46 GHz frequency band. The design of the amplifier circuits which utilize these devices is discussed. The circuit design is based on a 3-step closed form algorithm. The first step is a passive circuit characterization with an automatic network analyzer. In the second step, a computer is used to generate diode device lines. The third step is load line synthesis for predictable operation. The resulting performance is described. 2 W over a 2-GHz bandwidth was achieved simultaneously with minimum gain of 9 dB.

articleTitle: Tunable gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: At the present time the development of gyrotrons and related devices is being stimulated by the demand for high-power microwaves to heat tokamak plasmas to fusion temperatures and for new radar applications. The development of low-power gyrotrons and their applications has largely been ignored. At Sydney University we are developing such low-power devices for spectroscopy and plasma scattering.

articleTitle: A 140/220GHz radiometer for airborne imaging
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A dual frequency (140/220 GHz) radiometer has been designed, developed, and delivered to the Naval Research Laboratory. This instrument has been used to obtain the first airborne, high resolution, low noise, passive imagery at these frequencies. It features all solid state receiver components, remote switching/operation, dual IF channels, a 220 GHz subharmonic mixer, and quasi-optical RF diplexing.

articleTitle: Recent developments in metal-oxide-metal detector technology
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent progress in the use of the M-O-M detector as an optical or submillimeter nonlinear element is summarized. The theory of behavior will be considered, and a complete bibliography of M-O-M research and applications papers covering the 18 years since first disclosure will be made available.

articleTitle: A 750 mW high power CH3OH laser operating at 119 μm
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: As part of a program to measure the electron density on' the TFTR tokamak at Princeton University, a high power far-infrared (FIR) laser utilizing the 119 μm line of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH has been constructed. This laser will be used in a ten channel interferometer/polarimeter and must eventually drive 21 Schottky diode detectors simultaneously. Therefore emphasis has been placed on delivering as much FIR power as possible.

articleTitle: A broadband high power millimeter to centimeter spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A simple spectrometer is described for measuring directly both a high electric field (0.1 – 100 kV/cm) and wavelength over a broadband (0.1 – 10 cm). The combination of interference and gas breakdown are utilized in measuring the electric field and wavelength. Electron diffusion and the characteristic breakdown relation limit resolution of submillimeter wavelengths by requiring very high electric field (> 100 kV/cm).

articleTitle: Stability parameters of stable hooked-tip MOM point contact diode as MM wave and infrared detector-mixer
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A progress report is given on the hooked-tip MOM point contact diode with further stabilization based on control of oxide layer thickness, selection of the metal post material and waveguide packaging.

articleTitle: Microturbulence studies on text
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A multichannel far-infrared (FIR) scattering system has been installed on the TEXT device utilizing both heterodyne and homodyne detection techniques. The system has allowed the power spectra of microturbulence to be measured on a single tokamak discharge. The results confirm many of the characteristics observed in a number of previous experiments [1,2,3]. However, significant new results are presented for a variety of plasma conditions, thereby expanding our knowledge of transport phenomena in fusion plasmas.

articleTitle: Mode selective directional couplers in overmoded circular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Mode selective couplers for overmoded waveguides were developed for transmission line systems between gyrotrons and plasma experiments to measure the mode composition. The directional couplers are either based on constructive interference of wanted mode amplitudes or destructive interference of unwanted mode amplitudes. Four-hole cross couplers serve as monitors for the contents of asymmetric modes and the orientation of their field vectors in the circular waveguide.

articleTitle: A high energy D2O laser for plasma diagnostics
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An optically-pumped D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser with an unstable resonator has delivered pulses exceeding 1μs in duration at energies approaching 1J. It is pumped with a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser system comprising a hybrid oscillator and an electron-beam preionized amplifier used in a triple pass configuration and producing 500J.

articleTitle: Absorption of CH3OH around waveguide CO2 laser lines
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the present work we have performed a systematic investigation of the absorption of CH OH around each of the normal CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser lines. A waveguide configuration, offering extended tunability (240 or 300 MHz depending on the particular cavity lenght) has heen used for the laser. An optoacoustic cell, equipped with Stark plates, have been used for detecting the absorption. The suitability of waveguide CO laser as pump sources of FIR emissions was already recognized (1,2,3). In case of complex rotovibrational spectra, like for CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH, many different absorptions are accessible within the tuning range of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser line. Nevertheless new saturation techniques in the three level scheme (4) can be successfully applied to assign the different transitions. The aim of the present investigation is helping the generation of new optically pumped FIR laser lines and the understanding of already known and new discovered rotovibrational molecular transitions. In the following some particular case will be illustrated: 9-P(20). In Fig. la) the laser mode is shown. The optoacoustic recording (b) displays at least three different absorptions at −83,' + 1+9 and +121 MHz. Only the central one is accessible to conventional sources, by which no FIR emissions have been reported to date (5). The FIR line at 51.3 μm, previously reported by a TEA laser (6), is now pumped CW (Fig.le). The excellent CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser spectral purity allows the detection of the Transferred Lamb dip and the determination of the offset (sign and magnitude) of the pump transition.

articleTitle: Interferometric fir phase imaging of a tokamak plasma
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Multichannel phase imaging of dielectric objects has been demonstrated in the laboratory using a microbolometer detector array and 400 GHz carcinotron radiation cource. The application of this imaging system to perform single shot measurements of electron density profiles in a tokamak plasma is described. The primary advantages are increased spatial resolution together with a much simpler optical system.

articleTitle: High efficiency operation of a 140 GHz, pulsed gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The operation of a 140 GHz pulsed gyrotron will be described. Output powers as high as 175 kW have been generated, and total efficiencies approaching 36% have been achieved. A comparison with theoretical predictions will be made.

articleTitle: Single-mode efficiency in free-electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: For free-electron laser (FEL) devices with dilute and cold electron beams, an expression for the single-mode efficiency, ∊, is defined. The connection with the full (quantum mechanical) gain, G, is such that ∊/G is equal to the ratio of the total photon energy to the kinetic electron-beam energy “trapped” in the interaction volume V. Both ∊ and G are discussed quantitatively, using the example of a quantum model of the Smith-Purcell FEL: it is shown that unlike G, ∊ depends on the total photon energy trapped in V even in the classical regime.

articleTitle: Ear infrared reflectivity of KH2PO4 in the 10 – 420 K temperature range
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Infrared reflectivity spectra of KH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> have been recorded in the 10 – 420 K temperature range over the 20 – 400 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> spectral region. The ferroelectric phase (T < 123 K) has been especially emphasized. The spectra fitted by the coupleddamped-oscillator model confirm the existence of a temperature dependent low frequency (soft) mode. The model parameters are ploted vs T and a tentative microscopic interpretation is discussed.

articleTitle: Submillimeter-wave response in tunnel-type and bridge-type Josephson junction
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The study of the Josephson junction is a new field for optically-pumped submillimeter laser spectroscopy. We report submillimeter-wave techniques for this spectroscopy and experimental results on the Shapiro step.

articleTitle: Minimization of noise temperature for the hot-electron mixer
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The principal factors which limit the bandwidth and noise temperature of a hot-electron mixer have been calculated. The minimum mixer contribution to the effective noise temperature is found to be 33 T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Lattice</inf>. under matched conditions, in good agreement with previously published experiments.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and frequency pulling of a 140 GHz gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A harmonic mixer system has been used to measure the operating frequency of a pulsed, 140 GHz gyrotron. Bandwidths as low as 3 MHz, which is the instrumental limit, have been observed at both low and high power operation. The experimental and theoretical dependence of frequency on voltage, current and magnetic field will be described.

articleTitle: The submillimeter-wave and infrared heterodyne spectra of deuterated fluoroform (CDF3)
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have analyzed the submillimeter-wave (SMMW) and infrared (IR) spectra of the v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> band of the symmetric-top molecule CDF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Our heterodyne measurements on 22 SMMW laser emissions and 404 IR absorptions have been analyzed together with previous data to determine the molecular constants of the ground and v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> states. We predict over 300 new SMMW emission lines by optical pumping with nitrous oxide and isotopic carbon dioxide IR lasers.

articleTitle: Low-cost Fourier Transform Spectrometer using a Burleigh Inchworm
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) has evolved rapidly since the mid-1960's. Although the principles of FTS (based upon the Michelson interferometer) had been known for quite some time, it was the availability of fast computers, necessary for efficient transform of the raw data into a spectrum, which enabled the FTS to develop so rapidly. Prior to the advent of the FTS, most spectroscopy in the infrared and submillimeter region was performed using vacuum grating spectroscopy. The throughput (Jacquinot) and multiplex (Fellgett) advantages of the FTS meant a dramatic saving in experimental time. Spectra that took days or even weeks with grating spectrometers could be obtained within a few hours with FTS. Efficient, high resolution spectroscopy became possible and readily available.

articleTitle: 95-GHz radar instrumentation system
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Georgia Institute of Technology Engineering Experiment Station is developing a pulsed, coherent, high-power 95 GHz instrumentation radar employing an extended interaction amplifier (EIA) transmitter. The system (HIPCOR-95) is intended to provide millimeter wave instrumentation support to future reconnaissance, surveillance, and target acquisition programs. This paper describes the new technology which supports the development of such a radar and the characteristics and operating parameters of the system.

articleTitle: IR detection by depletion of trapped charge
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We describe a mode of infrared detection which involves the depletion of charge stored in localized states in semiconductors at low temperatures. This mode features very long integration times (up to 12 hours or more) and field-enhanced response beyond the usual long wavelength cutoff.

articleTitle: TE1,n gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Gyrotrons with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,n</inf> cavities can be configured to have a greater mode stability than gyrotrons with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o,n</inf> cavities. Two gyrotrons have been designed to use TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,3</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,6</inf> cavities to produce at 94 GHz approximately 0.5 MW and 1.25 MW,'respectively. Available experimental data will be presented.

articleTitle: The Fourier spectrometer ECE diagnostic system for the TFTR tokamak
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An electron cyclotron emission diagnostic based upon a commercial fast-scanning Michelson interferometer with a mirror reciprocation frequency of 36.5 Hz and spectral resolution of 3 GHz is being prepared. An overview of the light collection optics and the spectrometer will be given.

articleTitle: EPR in DAG at FIR wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Observation of paramagnetic resonance as a function of frequency allows the determination of the g-values in DAG, despite an unknown demagnetizing effect. To saturate the magnetization, high magnetic fields and thus FIR radiation are required.

articleTitle: Absolute measurement of electron cyclotron emission using radiometer with SIS tunnel junction
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Calibration of a W-band 8-channel heterodyne receiver for the measurement of the electron cyclotron emission (ECE) from W VII-A stellarator may be realized by adding a further channel with SIS mixer of high sensitivity as a reference in which ECE, attenuated to about 1000 K, is compared with the emission of well known blackbody sources at 77 K and 290 K.

articleTitle: Theory of a harmonic gyrotron in a rectangular cavity using a ribbon type electrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Small signal theory of a harmonic gyrotron operating in an axially grooved rectangular waveguide using a ribbon type electron beam will be presented. Mode selection and efficiency scaling as a function of harmonic number will be discussed.

articleTitle: New point-contact diodes for infrared heterodyne detection
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Experiments with point-contact diodes consisting of different combinations of metals, semimetals, and semiconductors to be used as laser harmonic generators and mixers up to 200 THz have resulted in three rugged devices: The W-Sb, W-SnTe, and W-Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> point contact diodes can partly replace the W-Ni and W-GaAs diodes respectively.

articleTitle: Recent Cerenkov maser experiments
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Fundamental (TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>) mode operation at 3 mm, and higher order mode operation at wavelengths below 1 mm, have been obtained in a recent series of Cerenkov maser experiments. Device performance will be compared with theoretical expectations.

articleTitle: Fraunhofer-diffraction method for plasma-wave measurements
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A generalized theory of the Fraunhofer-diffraction method (far-forward scattering) is proposed, which includes most practical conditions encountered in plasma-wave measurements, such as detections of position and propagating angle, and finite width of a plasma-wave, which have not been considered previously. Experimental verifications of the theory and general optics-design procedures for measurements of typical plasma-waves are presented.

articleTitle: Submillimeter mixing with Hg1-xCdxTe
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Mixing with Hg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te at submillimeter wavelengths is reported. It is shown that optimum performance depends critically on the x value chosen and the operating temperature. Bandwidths of more than 50 MHz have been obtained with x = 0.44 and temperature 3.2K.

articleTitle: Mode filtering in grating spectrometers at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Grating spectrometers employed as electron cyclotron emission diagnostic systems use as entrance and exit slits pieces of rectangular or circular waveguide with a scale size of 5 → 10λ. Since only the extraordinary mode polarization of the radiation is wanted, a wire grid polarizer is used to reject the other radiation. A combination of polarizer, finite size of slit, finite grating size, and limited etendue of the instrument severely limits the number of modes of the radiation field transmitted through the instrument.

articleTitle: EPR IN TmVO4 using an optically pumped fir laser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: To determine the g-value of the doublet ground state of the Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ion in TmVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, problems arise due to unknown local fields. Using FIR wavelengths these difficulties can be overcome. However, several unexplained resonances with different g-values were observed.

articleTitle: Observations of amplitude and angle of arrival scintillation in millimeter wave propagation caused by turbulence in clear air near the ground
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Observations were conducted over uniform, exceptionally flat farm land in Illinois during clear weather in July, 1983. Scintillation data were obtained at 116.30 and 172.91 GHz for a path 1.4 km long. Rigorous micrometeorological measurements, some of them path averaging, were made along the path. The results of these tests will be described.

articleTitle: Enhancement of high-harmdnic gyrotron gain by a dielectric rod
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A dielectric rod is shown to reduce the energy requirements of the electron beam for high-harmonic gyrotron operation. A large interaction filling factor can occur for moderate-energy electrons (∼ 80 keV) spiralling around the rod within the evanescent region of a dielectric waveguide mode. Since the magnetic field strength is reduced by an order of magnitude in an interaction at the tenth harmonic of the cyclotron frequency, a submillimeter-wave gyrotron is now truly feasible because the acceleration voltages can be conveniently produced by DC power supplies.

articleTitle: Wide-bandwidth HgCdTe photodiode photomixers at 28 μm
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Long-wavelength HgCdTe photodiodes operating at 20 K have been developed with quantum efficiencies >40%, bandwidths >500 MHz and a calculated heterodyne NEP = 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−20</sup> W/Hz for a local oscillator power of 100 μW at 28 μm. A theoretical analysis along with wavelength response, pulse response and noise data are described.

articleTitle: Dielectric constant determination at millimeter waves and elevated temperature
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A method is described for measuring dielectric constants of small cylindrical specimens using a waveguide reentrant cavity system at frequencies from 10GHz to 100GHz and from room temperature to 500°C.

articleTitle: A millimeter-wave system for the remote sensing of acidic clouds and precursor gases in the troposphere
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two millimeter-wave spectrometer systems are presented. The first operates in the 146–150 GHz and 162–166 GHz ranges, and is used to infer tropospheric abundances of COS, gaseous HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CO, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S, N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, all of which are gases closely related to the formation of acid precipitation. The second system operates in the 15 to 30 GHz range and would be used to infer acidity of tropospheric clouds.

articleTitle: Speckle phenomena at 10 um wavelength
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Scattering of radar and infra-red waves is strongly influenced by the multi-scale (fractal) nature of naturally-occurring surfaces. Measurements using CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser radiation illustrate striking differences between scattering by fractal and smoothly-varying surfaces. The influence of speckle in coherent laser radar will be discussed.

articleTitle: Medical microwave imagery: An inverse scattering approach
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An inverse scattering approach for image reconstruction is described. It is shown that, from measurements of the phase and amplitude of the electric field in one polarization using a water immersed microwave array one can obtain desirable focusing and resolution in both transverse and longitudinal directions.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of ordinary ray far infrared optical constants of sapphire
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The refractive index n + ik of c-cut sapphire at seven temperatures from 5.5 to 300 K has been measured between 30 and 230 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. The strongest temperature dependence occurs above 200 K for n and above 150 K for k. Evidence of multi-phonon processes was observed.

articleTitle: Indium phosphide millimeter-wave devices
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The use of InP for Gunn oscillators and amplifiers has recently led to a number of very useful products for millimeterwave applications. The ability to grow high purity indium phosphide material as required for Gunn effect devices and the increased understanding of the operation of both amplifier and oscillator diodes have lead to some significant improvements in the performance of these devices. CW efficiencies above 9% at 56 GHz and above 4.5% at 94 GHz have been obtained with these improved InP oscillator diodes. Average efficiencies of recent shipments of 56 GHz diodes are well above 6%. CW powers of over 250 mW have been obtained in the 53 GHz region.

articleTitle: Tunable far-infrared emission from uniaxial-stress-enhanced spin-flip transitions in InSb
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We report the first observation of far infrared emission resulting from spin-flip transitions in uniaxially stressed n-type InSb. The emission is generated by electrical exitation. The emission is tunable from 2 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> to 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and has a linewidth below 0.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. This is the narrowest linewidth of tunable electrically exited emitters reported so far.

articleTitle: Analysis of optically pumped CD3OH laser lines
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Assignments of FIR laser lines in optically pumped CD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH are described. Fermi resonance will occur in energy levels between n=0, τ=1, K=1 torsional levels of vibrational state and n=3,4 τ=1, K=1 levels of ground state. Discrepancy between the expected transition and the pump CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser frequencies of 10R(18) and 10R(8) is corrected by the introduction of the Fermi resonance. The calculated wavenumber of expected transition pumped by 10R(36) also is corrected with Fermi resonance in τ=3 K=9 torsional levels more accurately.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of beryllia in the near-millimeter wavelength range
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The refractive indices and absorption coefficients of four beryllia (BeO) ceramic samples have been measured between 4 and 18 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> with a Michelson interferometer. The index, n, follows a linear relationship with density, p, over the range 2.8 < p < 3.0 g/cc, and thus exhibits a density-dependent index variation of about 3 percent.

articleTitle: Accurate closed-form solutions for fin-lines
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Accurate closed-form expressions are derived for the theoretical prediction of equivalent dielectric constant, cutoff wavelength, and characteristic impedance of unilateral, bilateral and insulated fin-lines. The expressions developed on a physical basis are accurate to within ±0.6% and valid over the range of structural parameters 0 ≤ b/a ≤ 1, 1/32 ≤ d/b ≤ 1, and 1/32 ≤ s/a ≤ 1/4 (see Fig. 1).

articleTitle: Self-consistent RF field approach for complex cavity gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have extended the self-consistent RF field approach for gyrotron oscillators to the case of complex cavity devices which have an abrupt change in the resonator wall radius. This cavity configuration is of interest as a method of controlling mode competition in high power gyrotrons. Mode conversion at the resonator wall discontinuity is calculated using the method of Clarricoats. Application is made to the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>/TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">04</inf> complex cavity gyrotron experiment at NRL. Available results will be presented.

articleTitle: Radiometric investigation of millimeter wave emissions of surface foam
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A novel experimental technique employing artificial bubbles was used to investigate the emissivity of surface foam at 35 GHz. Improvement over previous research was achieved oy focusing the sensing antenna in the Rayleigh region and utilizing controlled bubbles. Experimental data show close agreement with the analytical bubble model.

articleTitle: The Orbitron Maser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The Orbitron Maser uses synthetic atoms in which free electrons orbit positively-charged metallic nuclei. These orbiting electrons interact with the radiation field of a microwave cavity to produce stimulated microwave emission. The difference between our device and ordinary microwave tubes and conventional masers is that it can operate in the difficult range between one centimeter and 0.1 millimeter.

articleTitle: Gyrotrons with special quasi-optical cavities
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Gyrotrons with special quasi-optical cavities have been proposed and the linear and nonlinear theories were formulated. theoretical study of these gyrotrons shows that they may have some advantages which make these gyrotrons have important significance in development of short-mm and sub-mm waves electron cyclotron resonance maser.

articleTitle: Isotropic conversion loss as a measure of quasi-optical mixer efficiency
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Conversion loss is an important practical measure of conventional mixer performance, but the usual definition of conversion loss is often inconvenient and inadequate when applied to quasi-optical mixers with integrated antennas. We herein define a new quantity called isotropic conversion loss (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">iso</inf>) which not only characterizes quasi-optical mixers with greater accuracy, but is also easier to measure in the laboratory. Experimental results from tests of two different mixers demonstrate the utility of the new measure L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">iso</inf>.

articleTitle: Far-infrared cyclotron resonance study of neutral impurity scattering in GaAs
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Photoexcited FIR laser cyclotron resonance has been able to separate electron-neutral donor and electron-neutral acceptor scattering rates in GaAs. The former is found to be nearly twenty times as large as the latter at 4.2 K.

articleTitle: Small target detection by space-borne radiometry
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The problem of radiometric detection from orbital platforms of small reflective targets against the sea surface is studied. Equations are developed to describe radiometric sensor signal-to-noise ratio in terms of orbital height, RF frequency, antenna diameter and other system parameters.

articleTitle: Operation of a high-hartonic gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The operation of a millimeter-wave harmonic gyrotron is described in which the interaction is between axis-encircling electrons and cylindrical cavity TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nll</inf> modes. Gyrotron cavities operating on this principle are well matched to low current, moderate energy, rfaccelerated electron beams. Efficiencies up to 15% have been measured for moderate harmonic interactions, multi-kW power levels have been attained at the eleventh harmonic of the cyclotron frequency, and 65 GHz waves have been produced. The concept allows the magnetic field of the gyrotron to be reduced by an order of magnitude, thereby making a submillimeter-wave gyrotron feasible. However, mode competition problems must be considered for high-harmonic, sub-millimeter wave operation, We have been successful in suppressing mode competition by destroying unwanted modes.

articleTitle: Convective cell formation in a gyro-traveling wave tube
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent work utilizing the relationship between solitons and convective cells to analytically model the nonlinear interaction dynamics of a gyro-traveling wave tube are presented. Theoretical predictions agree qualitatively with computer simulations and experimental data.

articleTitle: The mechanical design of a high-power, dual-frequency, millimeter-wave antenna feed system
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes the mechanical design and fabrication of a high power, dual-frequency, millimeter-wave feed system. The feed system consists of a 35 GHz circularly polarized monopulse subsystem and a 95 GHz circularly polarized feed. The 35 GHz feed is designed to handle 5.0 KW average power and the 95 GHz 1.2 KW average power. A Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) is incorporated to provide dual frequency capability. Each feed is liquid cooled to provide suitable cooling during high power of operation. The two feeds and FSS assembly are mounted in a supporting space frame to provide an optically integral assembly ready to be mounted at the vertex of a reflector. The paper addresses three main areas: the general feed design, which includes the manufacturing processes, flange considerations and waveguide cooling; the FSS fabrication; and beam alignment for both the primary and secondary fields.

articleTitle: Dielectric filters for short millimetre wave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Characteristics are presented for narrow. band pass (∼3%) filters designed with temperature compensated high permittivity dielectrics (barium nonatitanate). At W band both duroid and Z cut quartz microstrip substrates have been investigated and the insertion losses due to the various coupling fields are estimated to be ∼ 2 dB for 2 resonator filters and ∼ 3.5 dB for 3 resonator filters.

articleTitle: Infrared laser-diode emission of Pb1-xMnxS in high magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We report on the low-tempera ture IR-emission of Pb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>S-laser diodes in magnetic fields up to 15 T. The emission spectra split in four different transitions with superimposed mode structure. Line position, intensity and polarization can be tuned by temperature and magnetic field. The experimental results support strongly the existence of non-diagonal terms in the microscopic s-d-exchange in interaction.

articleTitle: Advances in microbolometers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The bismuth microbolometer is a simple, easily made detector suitable for use throughout the far-infrared. A novel photoresist fabrication procedure has made it possible to obtain an electrical NEP of 2.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup>W (Hz)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup> at 100kHz for an airbridge bolometer. By using a polyimide plastic as an insulator, conventional substrate-supported devices with an NEP of 3.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup>W(Hz)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup> have also been made.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave measurements of the TFTR line integrated density & electron temperature profile
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Millimeter — submillimeter wave diagnostics are expected to contribute to the characterization of the Tokamak Fusion Test Reactor (TFTR) plasma. The goal of TFTR is to demonstrate energy breakeven by generating fusion neutron power equal to the input power to the plasma. Plasma breakeven conditions includeg electron and ion temperatures on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> °K and plasma densities of n ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> particles/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Four millimeter-submillimeter instruments will diagnose the TFTR plasma: (1) 1mm wave density interferometer, (2) Fast Scanning heterodyne radiometer, (3) Fourier Transform Spectrometer, and (4) 1mm wave density scattering. With the exception of the scattering system, the design of these diagnostics were presented at the Sixth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> This past year the 1mm interferometer and the fast scanning heterodyne receiver have measured the line average density and the time evolution of the electron temperature profile of the TFTR plasma during its initial operation. The performance of these diagnostics will be presented including examples of plasma density and temperature measurements.

articleTitle: Production and study of axis circling electron beams for gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Production and analysis by two different techniques of axis circling beams will be discussed. The effect of field gradients on spatial spread of electrons including space charge effects will be given.

articleTitle: Analysis of a forward injection wideband traveling wave amplifier
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Theoretical results will be presented for a wideband forward injection gyrotron traveling wave amplifier. The wideband frequency spectrum is obtained by employing a weakly tapered external magnetic field which is set above exact grazing. Operation at such magnetic fields has been demonstrated by initial experimental observations. It will be shown that, in spite of a large launching loss over the whole frequency region, it is possible to obtain significant gain over a broad bandwidth. Also, it will be shown that the absolute instability, that usually occurs in the gyrotron traveling wave amplifier, can be avoided by operating at a high beam voltage. Finally, results on the effect of temperature on the performance of the device will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of a D2O laser pumped by an injection-locked TEA CO2 laser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In order to perform collective Thomson scattering measurements of ion temperature in Tokamak plasmas, a high-power, narrow-band submillimeter (SMM) laser, which is optically pumped by a tunable, single-mode injection-locked TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser, is now being developed.

articleTitle: Fin-line PIN-diode attenuator and switch for the 140 GHz range
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A PIN-diode attenuator and switch is being described for the 140 GHz range with broadband characteristics. The switch works between 130 GHz and 145 GHz with a maximum insertion loss of 2 dB in the “ON”-state and minimum isolation of 25 dB in the “OFF”-state.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of impact — ionized plasma instability in GaAs
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Impact ionization delay time in GaAs is estimated by Monte Carlo technique. The linear regime of the instability caused by the ionization delay is investigated. The nonlinear stage of this instability is numerically simulated. The instability frequency is obtained within the range of 50 + 1000 GHz.

articleTitle: Discontinuous MIM film chip arrays as MM wave and infrared detector-mixer diodes
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Marked improvement is reported on the responsitivity and power handling capability of discontinuous MIM film diodes when deposited as IC chip arrays with microwave and infrared waveguide packaging and tuning.

articleTitle: 25 Years of millimeter plasma diagnostic systems
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The paper will cover the author's experience with millimeter plasma diagnostic systems during the past twenty-five years at the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory. Comparisons will be made of the various microwave components and RF sources that were used from the late 1950's up to the present time. The systems requirements and data acquisition methods over the period will also be compared.

articleTitle: High power pure rotational laser due to vibrational excitation
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: It is suggested for the first time to use VRT-relaxation for the excitation of high power laser action on rotational transitions in FIR spectral range. It is shown, that the required conditions can be achieved by the free expansion of the previosly heated mixture of hydrogen ha lides molecules and slowly relaxing molecules.

articleTitle: Ion Bernstein wave studies on microtor
