publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In recent years heating in the ion cyclotron range of frequency (ICRF) has been under active study as an efficient source of supplementary heating in tokamak plasmas. At UCLA far-infrared (FIR) collective Thomson scattering has been employed to directly probe and identify the various plasma waves, thereby improving the understanding of ICRF wave physics. In addition, the measurement of the dispersion of externally excited ion Bernstein waves has resulted in a determination of ion temperature at a number of radial locations. The ion Bernstein waves are identified as being generated through mode conversion of the fast magnetosonic wave at the second harmonic ion cyclotron layer.

articleTitle: SIS mixer in 3-port approximation from an experimental I-V curve
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Conversion efficiency and output conductance are calculated on the basis of an experimental I-V characteristic of a lead alloy tunnel junction in the 3-port approximation considering both the junction capacitance and the quantum reactance. Gain is found only when the reactances are nearly completely tuned out, otherwise loss of at least 7 dB is expected under usual practical conditions. The calculations have been carried out for local oscillator frequency of 88 GHz in the limit of low intermediate frequency.

articleTitle: Modification of microturbulence during impurity injection on text
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A multichannel, far-infrared (FIR) laser scattering system is used to study the temporal development of the power spectra of low frequency microturbulence in the TEXT tokamak. The single shot measurement capability has revealed significant modifications in the spectra during laser ablative injection of small quantities of scandium into the plasma. The present paper reports these observations in detail and discusses their relevance to transport phenomena in fusion plasmas.

articleTitle: Conversion of gyrotron TEon-mode mixtures into a linearly polarized HE11 wave
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This work reports measurements on mode converters to transform circular electric gyrotron TEg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>-mode compositions (mainly TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf>) into the linearly polarized hybrid HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> wave which is in many respects ideal for use in quasioptical launching systems for electron cyclotron resonance plasma heating by means of high power gyrotrons. Periodically modulated wall mode converter sections (sinusoidal m=0 radius modulation) convert TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> mode mixtures into a nearly pure TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode with a measured efficiency of about 98 % at 28 GHz. The TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> wave is used for long distance transmission through smooth overmoded waveguideswith optimized tapers and corrugated bends. In a second converter with constant diameter and periodically modulated curvature in one plane (m=1 distortion) the circular symmetric TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode is transferred into the nearly linearly polarized TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode with an efficiency of about 97 %. The Gaussian HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode with almost no cross-polarization is produced in a circumferentially corrugated TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> to HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converter. The overall efficiency of the complete microwave system is about 90 %.

articleTitle: A helium cooled michelson interferometer for far infrared astronomy on spacelab
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Spectroscopy of astronomical objects in the mid- and far-infrared region will contribute substantially to our understanding of basic astrophysical processes (e.g. formation of stars and galaxies). Today, a number of intense lines have been detected in the brightest sources (mainly HII regions) using airborne and balloon-borne telescopes with equipments at ambient temperatures.

articleTitle: Granular superconducting NbN films as submillimeter detectors
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Non-bolometric detection is observed in granular superconducting NbN films. Detection, related to the non-linear I-V's, occures over a large bias range. Preliminary results give a sensitivity of 20 V/W and NEP of 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>W at 4 K. Granular NbN films show no apparent degradation with time.

articleTitle: Surface current analysis of a corner cube mixer
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The surface current is described for a long wire antenna located in a corner cube. The ground plane perpendicular to the wire is found to be unimportant to the operation of the antenna. Detailed calculations are made for the roof-top reflector configuration which show the importance of obstructions near the apex of the reflector.

articleTitle: Frequency detuning measurements in a low power gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The operating frequency of a gyrotron is largely determined by the resonant frequency of the cavity. For example, with a cathode-resonator voltage of 19 kV and a beam current of 40 mA, Sydney University Gyrotron II can oscillate in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0 14 1</inf> cavity mode as long as the gyrofrequency is in the range from 181.15 GHz to 182.91 GHz. However, the operating frequency will never move more than a few tens of megahertz away from the resonant frequency of the cavity, 182.99 GHz.

articleTitle: The source of a problem with rapid-scanning fourier transform spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In this paper, a difficulty with rapid-scanning interferometers will be discussed. By “rapid-scanning interferometer” is meant one which uses no chopper or lock-in amplifier in the data-acquisition system. Instead, the moving mirror is scanned at a constant velocity, making the infrared intensity at the detector be modulated in the audio frequency range. The signal from the detector is amplified by a broadband amplifier and digitized for later processing by a computer. This technique has advantages over the “step and integrate” procedure insofar as simplicity of interferometer drive, noise reduction, and suppression of long-term drifts in source or detector are concerned.

articleTitle: Development of terrestrial millimeter-wave communications
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Point-to-point millimeter-wave communications have now been extensively developed. This presentation will summarize the applications and give state-of-the-art performance for several examples at frequencies above 30 GHz. Particular emphasis will be placed on the parameters of multi-channel, solid state systems operating in the 36 to 38.6 GHz and 54 to 60 GHz regions.

articleTitle: Submillimeter detection with Hg1-xCdxTe
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In recent papers [1] and [2] Weber and Kulpa have reported on the usefulness of the alloy semiconductor Hg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te as a long wavelength electron bolometer detector. Although our main interest is in the use of this semiconductor as a mixer for far infrared heterodyne experiments [3], we have inevitably also studied its wider response. Although this research is at a fairly early stage, and some of the results are not easy to interpret, our best detector has a good detectivity (NEP < 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup> WHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−½</sup> at 500 μm and < 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup> WHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−½</sup> at 900 μm), with a significantly faster response than n-InSb. Moreover, construction of the detector is very simple compared with n-InSb where considerable ingenuity is required to make high impedance, high voltage responsivity detectors without employing magnetic fields.

articleTitle: A new W-band waveguide Gunn oscillator
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: An improved waveguide oscillator structure is presented. This oscillator circuit provides a high degree of tunability with a sliding back short and an adjustable sliding iris incorporated into one structure. Results are presented for a W-band Gunn oscillator prototype, demonstrating improved frequency stability-compared to a commercially available W-band Gunn oscillator and to a W-band klystron.

articleTitle: Simultaneous FIR interferometry/polarimetry in the UCLA Microtor plasma
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Faraday rotation and electron line density spatial profiles ahve been measured simultaneously on the Microtor tokamak using the phase modulation scheme originally proposed by Dodel and Kunz [1]. Presently, a single channel system is spatially scanned across the complete plasma profile at 1 cm intervals. The extension of this technique to a 20 channel interferometer/polarimeter system using micro-bolometer imaging arrays is briefly described together with an assessment of the importance of such a system on fusion plasmas.

articleTitle: Design of high power gyrotron oscillators with complex cavity structure
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Currently, experiments are in preparation at Hughes Aircraft Co. and at NRL for the generation of high power by means of the gyrotron oscillator. Theoretical results will be presented on the design and performance of the two high power gyrotrons that will be used in these experiments. Both resonant structures employ a complex cavity configuration which was conceived to alleviate the problem of mode competition. The first gyrotron consists of a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">031</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">041</inf> combination with an output power of 0.5 MW, while the second gyrotron consists of a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">031</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">061</inf> combination with an output power of 1 MW. Both gyrotrons operate at 100 GHz. Results will be presented on the starting currents in the presence of magnetic tapering and on the optimal operating conditions of each device.

articleTitle: Pure rotational spectroscopy of SO2 using fix line far infrared lasers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have identified approximately 86 near-coincidences between calculated SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pure rotational transitions and known FIR laser lines. Stark modulation and pressure broadening studies on 15 coincidences with the methanol laser lines have been carried out. Differences between measured and calculated frequencies have been observed with higher K quantum number transitions systematically appearinq at frequencies lower than calculated. An almost exact match has been observed between the methanol 163.1 μ line and the SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (25<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14,12</inf> ← 24<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13,11</inf>) transition, occurrinq approximately'80 MHz below its calculated frequency. This observation will allow the development of a laser based monitor of trace SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in gaseous mixtures.

articleTitle: Cyclotron harmonic maser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Recent experiments will be discussed in which coherent power has been extracted from a gyrotron-like device up to the ninth cyclotron harmonic, and at wavelengths (in a single device) ranging from 8 mm to below 1 mm. The device employs a solid-beam 20 kV Pierce gun, a magnetostatic kicker, and a combination of two confocal Fabry-Perot resonators. Evidence supports the interpretation that high harmonic oscillations occur because coupling occurs at the beam boundary allowing short-wavelength Bernstein modes to be excited on the beam.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Implications of these results will be drawn for the design of compact tunable mm-wave and sub-mm wave sources, and/or for mm-wave devices not requiring superconducting magnets.

articleTitle: Detection at 100–300 μm with Hg1-xCdxTe in a magnetic field
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: At the 7th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves, Weber and Kulpa (in a distributed paper) reported enhanced response of a HgCdTe detector when operated in magnetic fields up to 30 kilogauss. However, unlike in n-InSb [1] hot electron bolometers there was no marked increase in responsivity at shorter far infrared wavelengths (compared with longer wave inhancement) with increasing field and no tunable response.

articleTitle: Extended interaction oscillator/amplifier modulator technology
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Extended Interaction Oscillators and Amplifiers (EIO/A) have proven to be reliable high power sources of millimeter waves.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> Their unique capabilities have been demonstrated in various modulator configurations. Proper selection and tailoring of the modulator will define the capability of the EIO/A to meet the requirements of the radar system. This paper describes the basic characteristics of the EIO/A, the typical modulator configurations developed to drive the EIO/A, and comparative results attained by each method.

articleTitle: Fast FIR laser interferometry for density fluctuation measurements in tokamak plasmas
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A fast FIR laser interferometry technique, using CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-pumped CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>I lasers at 447 μm, is employed in the Petula B tokamak to diagnose low-frequency (ω << ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ci</inf>) electron-density fluctuations. Digitally implemented FFT and coherence analyses are made to determine various characteristics of the fluctuations.

articleTitle: Paper sheet moisture measurements in the far infrared
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The reflectance and transmittance of paper sheets have been measured as a function of moisture content at several wavelengths between 70 and 570 μm. Potential applications in the pulp and paper industry are discussed.

articleTitle: The atmospheric water vapor continuum below 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Absolute attenuation rates due to water vapor and moist nitrogen have been measured in the laboratory at 138 GHz, 282 and 300 K, pressures up to 1.5 atm, and relative humidities from 80 to 100 percent. The computer-controlled measuring system is comprised of a millimeter wave resonance spectrometer (0.15 km effective path length) and a humidity simulator. Several shortcomings of earlier measurement attempts have been rectified. The data are interpreted as a water vapor continuum spectrum consisting of two terms, namely strong self-broadening(H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O) plus foreign-gas-broadening (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) contributions. Implications of the new results for modeling atmospheric EHF window transparencies are discussed.

articleTitle: Submillimeter wave Schottky-barrier diode with a buried Pt/GaAs-alloy anode
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Schottky-barrier diodes for use at submillimeter wavelengths have been fabricated by using the solid-solid reaction between Pt and n-GaAs. The sub-millimeter wave detection- and noise-characteristics of the diodes will be presented.

articleTitle: EHF satellite communications technology — transmitters and receivers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: During the past three years, interest in satellite communications in the frequency bands above Ku-band has expanded dramatically. As a result, a number of key technology developments, targeted to meet specific next generation spaceborne needs, were undertaken. The state-of-the-art in solid state power transmitters and low noise receivers, including critical passive component technology, is presented. This included filters as well as a series of rugged high performance ferrite components such as isolators, circulators and latching switches.

articleTitle: Calibration techniques for broadband MM & SMMW diagnostic instruments
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Absolute calibration of electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostics allows for the determination of temporal electron temperature measurements independent of other diagnostics. Calibration of MM and SMMW diagnostics with a blackbody of known temperature using synchronous detection and co-adding techniques is described.

articleTitle: Conference abstract: Cryogenic operation of a broadband open structure mixer for the submillimeter wavelength range
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A cooled quasi optical submillimeter mixer using GaAs Schottky barrier diode in an open structure mount has been developed for operation at 20 K. Tunability between 300 and 900 GHz is permitted even at cryogenic temperatures. Measurements of the temperature dependence of mixer conversion loss, noise temperature, diode inverse slope parameter, saturation current and series resistance will be presented.

articleTitle: Sub-mm and millimeter observations of the outer planets
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Using the UKIRT and NRAO telescopes we have observed Uranus and Neptune in six filter bandpasses from 0.35 to 2.0 mm. Atmospheric structure models fit the results for Neptune but not Uranus. We speculate that an unknown constituent affects the Uranian Near-mm emmission.

articleTitle: Harmonic emission from high frequency gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Second harmonic emission of power levels of ≳ 25 kW and frequencies up to 302 GHz have been achieved in a short pulse gyrotron designed for operation at the fundamental in the 110–170 GHz band. Frequency, starting current and power level measurements for several harmonic modes have been made. A theoretical analysis of harmonic content is discussed and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Triple resonance on the CH3OH laser: Asymmetry splittings and new lines
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the optically pumped far-infrared (FIR) laser an oscillating field can be applied directly on the laser medium. A resonance between a tunable RF field and any transition connected to one of the levels of the laser cycle will be detected as a change in the output power. Fig. 1 shows the three possible cases. Transition 1 decreases the output power, which is on the contrary, increased by transitions 2 and 3, even if the signal is smaller in these latter cases. Such an experiment is more conveniently referred to as a triple resonance (TR) experiment because of the simultaneous presence of three coherent radiation fields. The feasibility of TR was demonstrated in HCOOH (1) and CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH (2,3) FIR lasers.

articleTitle: An improved acousto optic laser scanner guidance system
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: There is an increasing demand for guidance systems capable of operating in a hostile ECM environment without the use of wire or similar links. This paper outlines such a system where a high speed laser transmitter scans a laser beam in a rectangular pattern across a receiver which is facing the transmitter. The system design is such that an object can determine its position accurately within the laser beam pattern without requiring a separate source of synchronising pulses or transmitter timing sequence information.

articleTitle: Synchrotron radiation as an infra-red source
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The characteristics of synchrotron radiation (SR) from dipole magnets in the infra-red are discussed. Compared with a black-body radiator, SR is some 2–3 orders of magnitude brighter in the range 1–1000 μm.

articleTitle: A free-space millimeter-wave dielectrometer for characterization of lossy materials
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A millimeter-wave (MMW) dielectrometer is being developed for the measurement of lossy magnetic and dielectric materials. It utilizes a single-pass, free-space bridge. Preliminary tests at 45 GHz have demonstrated the ability of this system to determine complex permittivity and permeability.

articleTitle: Subnanosecond optical switching of far infrared radiation
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Switching of 119 μn CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH laser radiation in less than 1 ns was achieved by irradiating high resistivity Si and GaAs samples with 1.4 ns, 150 μJ pulses from a 337 nm TEA nitrogen laser. Modulation degrees of up to 100 % were observed both in reflection and transmission.

articleTitle: Design, manufacture and transmission measurements of strip gratings for use as sub-millimeter laser couplers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We present a simple method for the design and manufacture of strip gratings placed on a dielectric substrate. Once the required transmittance is specified, the dimension of the grating may be determined using simple formulae based on rigorous diffraction theory. The strip gratings are first drawn on photographic film using a newly developed light pen plotter. The grating is then photographically reduced to the final size and transferred to the substrate by photolithography. A teflon anti-reflection coating is placed on the back of the substrate to reduce multiple reflections. Measurements of transmittance are presented and show good agreement with theory.

articleTitle: A three-channel 3He-cooled Bolometer for sub-mm balloon spectroscopy of the stratosphere
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Two recent flights in the International Balloon Intercomparison Campaign have provided improved high resolution (0.003cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) spectra of the stratoshperic emission. The instrument performance was improved greatly in the 20–50cm range compared to the 1979 flight by the use of detectors operated at 0.3 Kelvin.

articleTitle: CH3OH laser line assignments revisited
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH line frequencies calculated by diagonalizing the molecular Hamiltonian are affected by inaccuracies of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> or higher, the inaccuracy increasing with the values of the quantum numbers involved in the line. The main sources of inaccuracy are the computational approximations and the fact that the best available molecular constants have beer evaluated from best fits of microwave data, which usually involve low quantum numbers only. These inaccuracies and the richness of the methanol spectrum generate several ambiguities in the line assignments, in particular in the assignment of the far infrared (FIR) lines of the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH laser. In order to overcome these ambiguities we have started a systematic investigation of the Fourier absorption spectrum of methanol in the regions between 8 and 80 and between 950 and 1100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. The peak precisions of our Fourier spectra are 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> and 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> respectively for the two spectral regions (1). With such precisions and with definite assignments for the absorption lines it is possible to form loops of lines containing at least three absorption lines and closed by an investigated laser line. The balance of the frequencies involved in the loop must give zero within the experimental errors, this leading practically always to a unique choice for the assignment of the laser line. We have thus been able to prove or disprove several previous assignments, to make new assignments and to predict the frequencies of some possible FIR laser lines not yet observed.

articleTitle: Multimode phenomena in optically-pumped lasers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Multimode phenomena in optically-pumped lasers are studied by means of Lamb's semi-classical theory. Specifically we investigate competition between Raman and line center oscillation in off-resonantly pumped FIR lasers. The observed preference of the Raman line is shown to be the result of an inversion of the line center gain for a moderate to high intensity Raman mode.

articleTitle: Analysis of the output mode from 60 GHz, 200 kW pulsed and CW gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A Varian 60 GHz, CW gyrotron has recently been operated at power levels up to 200 kW CW. The tube employs a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</inf>/TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">021</inf> complex interaction cavity which inhibits mode competition by the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">221</inf> mode with the desired TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">021</inf> mode. The output mode of the cavity is nominally in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> circular waveguide mode in overmoded waveguide. Since the output waveguide also serves as the gyrotron collector, mode conversion occurs in the taper sections and gaps incorporated into the collector. Measurements of the mode conversion on a 60 GHz, 200 kw, 100 ms pulse tube, have been made and compared with similar measurements on the 60 GHz, 200 kW, CW gyrotron. These measurements indicated that the CW tube had significantly more conversion of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode into other TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> modes than did the pulse tube. Current design work is aimed at reducing the mode conversion of the CW design to the same levels as the pulse design (≲10% mode conversion).

articleTitle: Studies of non-reciprocal effects in planar near-millimeter waveguiding structure: Analysis of a 5-region canonical structure with 2 semiconducting slabs
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We present here the first results of an analytical and numerical study of a five-region planar canonical structure which models non-reciprocal devices for the near-millimeter wave range using surface magnetoplasmon modes. The model includes two slabs of high quality semiconducting material, such as n-GaAs, independently magnetized parallel to the interfaces and perpendicular to the direction of propagation. This analysis in an extension of the one performed in reference 1. Emphasis is placed on a discussion of the results and we suggest directions for further research.

articleTitle: Long-Pulse, high-current free electron laser with no external focusing
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A 2-μ sec-duration electron beam from an induction linac is used to drive a free electron laser (FEL). Experiments using a helical wiggler without any external focusing have made possible an unambiguous study of the FEL radiation. Power levels of 2–4 MW have been measured at ∼ 30 GHz, corresponding to an interaction efficiency of 1.5–3%.

articleTitle: Cavity design for a two-stage FEL
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In the KMS Fusion two-stage free electron laser (FEL) experiment, the first-stage and second-stage radiation must suffer low losses in the oscillator. The electromagnetic modes overlap each other (and the electron beam) in a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> waveguide but separate before reaching the end mirrors.

articleTitle: Mode selective high power measurements on a 28 GHz gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">om</inf> mode composition of a Varian 28 GHz pulse gyrotron was measured with mode selective directional couplers. Of special interest are also the mostly neglected asymmetric modes and their changes of polarization with modified operational parameters of the gyrotron; these measurements were perfomed by a four-hole cross coupler.

articleTitle: Resonant Tunneling through quantum wells up to 2.5 THz
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have observed resonant tunneling through a single quantum well of GaAs between two barriers of GaAlAs. The current singularity and negative resistance region are dramatically improved over previous results. Approximate agreement with a simple theory has been obtained. Detection and mixing experiments carried out at frequencies as high as 2.5 THz show the intrinsic response time to be less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−13</sup> sec.

articleTitle: Parabolic tapers for overmoded waveguides
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Waveguide tapers in which axial position is proportional to the tapered dimension squared can be synthesized from virtually exact solutions of the coupled mode equations. Such tapers have much less mode conversion over narrow bands than equal length linear tapers. The minimum length required to produce a null in the mode conversion is also shorter than that for other nonlinear tapers.

articleTitle: Simplified small signal gain calculations in free electron lasers
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A method proposed recently<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup> is used for the evaluation of the small signal gain in various free electron laser configurations. The theory is applied to (a) the wiggler-free free electron laser with a uniform axial guide magnetic field and arbitrary direction of propagation of the amplified radiation and (b) the free electron laser with the axially modulated guide field (lowbitron<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup>). It is demonstrated that the new approach simplifies the gain calculation significantly in comparison with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Integrated circuit components and receivers for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: This paper describes the performance of various millimeter-wave planar integrated circuit components including mixers, Gunn VCOs, frequency multipliers, switches, attenuators, filters and couplers. Using these components as building blocks, several receiver front-end systems have been built at Ka-, V- and W-band.

articleTitle: Magnetooptical investigations of intraband transitions in n-Pb1-xMnxTe
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We report on the observation of intraband magneto-optical transitions in n-Pb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te (0 ≤ × ≤ 0.02) in epitaxial film of high carrier mobility (μ ∼ 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs) in magnetic fields up to 20 T. Among the observed resonance transitions the cyclotron resonance and combined resonance were identified. The g-tensor is not proportional to the macroscopic magnetization in its T- and B-dependence. In addition, transitions are observed which extrapolate to a finite binding energy.

articleTitle: Broadband slot-ring balanced mixer for millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We have developed a prototype model for a new type of mixer, which is suitable for integrated receivers using endfire tapered slot antennas. The mixer uses a slot-ring balanced configuration with a slotline input, directly connectable to the antenna. Model measurements show conversion loss less than 6 dB over an octave bandwidth.

articleTitle: A cryogenic mixer receiver for submillimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A low noise receiver for 350 GHz is described, using a Schottky diode mixer and FET amplifier operating at 20 K. Local oscillator power is provided by a frequency tripler., The best receiver temperature is 1050 K at 348 GHz. The same mixer design has been sucessfully scaled for room temperature operation at 530 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic behavior of a fir waveguide laser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: We consider the discrete and the continuous modes in hollow slab and cylindrical waveguides. We compute the transmission and reflection coefficients by a mode matching method. The oscillation conditions are determined for each mode.

articleTitle: Fin-line components and subsystems for use above 90 GHz
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A summary of realized planar mm-wave fin-line components and integrated front-ends for frequencies up to 150 GHz is presented. This includes couplers, PIN-diode attenuators, switches, balanced mixers, and detectors as well as integrated combinations of them.

articleTitle: Nonlinear MM wave generation in a planar structure containing semiconductor
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: In this paper we examine the problem of EM wave generation using nonlinear mixing schemes. The structure to be analyzed is shown in Fig. 1. It consists of layers of differing dielectrics, some of which may be doped or undoped GaAs materials. It is symmetric about the center plane and is infinite and uniform in the direction transverse to the normal ○ and the direction of propagation z. In the center is a thin layer of single crystal GaAs material which exhibits optical nonlinearity. The nonlinearity consists of the contributions from both the valence electrons of the intrinsic GaAs material and the conduction electrons introduced into the medium by external means. Two optical waves propagating inside the center layer induce, as a result of optical mixing, a distribution of electric dipoles which radiate EM waves at the sum, difference or harmonic frequencies of the input waves. We are particularly interested in the generation of waves at the difference frequency which, for two CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser inputs, ranges from ∼150–4000 GHz. The dispersion characteristic and field distribution of the excited waves are determined by the waveguiding property of the whole structure at that frequency.

articleTitle: A study of the F.I.R. stress induced photoconductivity in gallium doped Germanium
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A simple instrument for the study of stress induced photoconductivity at 4.2 K is described. The specimen is mounted between sapphire and copper berylium anvils and illuminated through the sapphire. Performance is illustrated by the results of broad band measurements on gallium doped germanium.

articleTitle: Simulation of high harmonic gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: The theory and numerical simulation of gyrotron devices operating in the Whispering Gallery TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m11</inf> mode will be discussed. A variety of devices, including the gyrotron oscillator, gyroklystron amplifier, and gyroresonant accelerator will be considered.

articleTitle: Design of slowwave broadband gyro-TWT with a bifilar helix circuit
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: By analyzing the Maxwell-Vlasov equations, a beam-wave dispersion relation has been derived for a gyro-TWT incorporating a bifilar helix slow-wave circuit. The linear gain has been examined in the slow-wave region to characterize anticipated performance. Results will be compared with that of the gyro-TWT with dielectric clad waveguide circuit.

articleTitle: Characterization of a dual-mode horn for submillimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A simple dual-mode conical horn has been developed and tested at 0.5 mm, 1.4 mm, 3.1 mm, and 34.2 mm. The horn has nearly equal beam shape in the E and H plane far field patterns with a 3dB half angle of 6°. At 34.2 mm the waveguide reflection loss and the phase center have been determined.

articleTitle: Infrared reflectivity of InGaAsP grown by molecular beam epitaxy
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Considerable interest has developed over the last few years in the application of In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>As<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</inf> alloys as diode laser sources and detectors for optical fiber communication systems. The importance of the In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>As<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</inf> alloy system stems from the fact that the band-gap and lattice constant can be adjusted independently using the composition parameters x and y. This enables the lasing wavelength to be adjusted for a specific application whilst, at the same time, ensuring lattice matched growth to InP and/or GaAs substrates.

articleTitle: Observation of Thomson scattering from ion thermal fluctuations in a tokamak plasma with a 385μm laser
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: Thomson scattering from ion thermal fluctuations in a tokamak plasma has been observed for the first time using a 385μm D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser system on Alcator C. The frequency shift of the scattered radiation was consistent with ion temperatures between 0.7 and 1.5 KeV. Experimental accuracy was limited by stray light caused by restricted port access.

articleTitle: Generation of high frequency radiation by quasi-optical gyrotron at harmonics of the cyclotron frequency
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A quasi-optical cavity is designed for harmonic operation of gyrotrons. Lower harmonics are suppressed by exploiting their larger diffraction losses, and the field amplitude is kept below the breakdown value by taking advantage of the focusing properties of the radiation in the resonator.

articleTitle: Design and operation of a high-harmonic gyro-klystron amplifier
publicationTitle: 1983 Eighth International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves
abstract: A gyro-klystron amplifier has been designed for operation at the sixth cyclotron harmonic. The system should exhibit 36 dB gain for 2.5 A rf-accelerated electron beams. Approximately 5 W are required for complete bunching to yield 20 kV?. The initial experiments, performed in the low current regime, have verified the theoretical I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> dependence of gain.
